items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I worked so hard there, Stanley, I swore when I went to be a man I'd never work again.

ctx.x: German, yeah. And they were all mixed up, you know. In fact, there was a little city in Kentucky, there were so many Schultzs there they named it Schultztown. That was my mother's parents. And during that span of time in Kentucky, my uncle was a coal miner and a farmer, you know. Everything that we ate, everything that we accumulated, so far as the house was concerned, was grown, you know. And I worked so hard there, Stanley, I swore when I went to be a man I'd never work again.
What sort of work did you do?
